Items.Authors: Roberto Pizzo, Hanno Holties, Marco Iacobelli, Emanuela Orrú, Aras Bozkurt
Items.Title: The LOFAR2.0 data challenge and current solutions
Items.Abstract: LOFAR is a high throughput data facility facing several non-trivial technical challenges in data processing, storage, and operations. The array is being upgraded to LOFAR2.0. The new system will offer several functionality improvements to the users, but will also pose unprecedented challenges related to the data handling, processing, storage and sustainable operations in general. In this talk, we will review these along with the solutions we have adopted to tackle them, including data compression, the retirement of the early LOFAR Cycle data, and the implementation of a LOFAR2.0 data lifecycle policy requiring the preservation of only advanced data products. Moreover, we will discuss the role of the community towards realizing more efficient data processing pipelines and scaling up the processing infrastructure. Eventually, we will review the actions undertaken to automate key areas of the intensive data handling chain to realize sustainable operations for the future.

Items.Authors: Sébastien Pernecker, Tarik Ibrahimovic, Jean-Paul Kneib, Jonathan Wei, Maxime Rombach, Oliver Pineda Suárez
Items.Title: Advancing control electronics for next-generation astronomical fiber robotic positioners
Items.Abstract: Next-generation spectroscopic surveys require compact, high-density fiber robotic positioner systems with 5μm precision, imposing strict size and power constraints on control electronics. We present a compact architecture driving 21 theta-phi SCARA positioners (42 BLDC motors) on a single board—a significant increase over current surveys like SDSS-V and DESI, where each positioner uses dedicated hardware. The design integrates power distribution, CAN communication, and synchronized motion control. It features sensorless Field-Oriented Control with collision detection and hard-stop calibration, reducing cost and complexity. We demonstrate that this module meets precision requirements while improving electronics densification and energy efficiency for future survey instruments.

Items.Authors: Shravan Menon, Kun Hu, Henric Krawczynski, Fabian Kislat
Items.Title: Design of a next-generation imaging hard x-ray polarimeter
Items.Abstract: X-ray polarimetry has emerged as a pivotal tool for investigating the inner workings of compact celestial objects such as accreting black-hole systems, rotation and accretion powered neutron stars, and magnetars. The Imaging X-Ray Polarimeter Explorer (IXPE) and the XL-Calibur missions have demonstrated the feasibility of X-ray polarimetry and shown that X-ray polarimetry makes substantial contributions to revealing the inner workings of these sources. The success of these missions motivate the development of a follow-up mission with improved sensitivity. We present the design and development of a new imaging hard X-ray polarimeter working over the broad energy range from 5 to 80 keV. The polarimeter offers excellent sensitivity for non-imaging polarimetry from 5 keV to 40 keV, and enables imaging polarimetry above 40 keV. We also discuss the possibility to combine it with other polarimeters to achieve an even broader bandpass.

Items.Authors: Yousef Chahine, Chaohan Cui, William DeRocco, Daniel Gottesman, Saikat Guha, Emil T. Khabiboulline, Zhenning Liu, Brittany M. McClinton, Jayadev Rajagopal, Fredrik T. Rantakyro, J. Gabriel Richardson, Stephen T. Ridgway, Aqil Sajjad, Joohyung Song
Items.Title: Eliminating photon transport in long-baseline optical interferometry using quantum memories
Items.Abstract: Current optical interferometers reach baselines up to ~ 300m, but many targets (e.g., stars, galactic nuclei, exoplanets) would benefit from considerably longer, even multi-km, baselines.     Classical approaches require: transmission of light over large distances for beam recombination; an extreme precision continuously variable optical delay line; and overcoming low throughput.     Quantum methods offer a new path. In this talk, we present the fundamental operating mechanisms of optical interferometry using quantum memory and entanglement. We show how these overcome the need for direct wavefront recombination, remove the optical delay line bottleneck, and offer possible improvements in system efficiency. We highlight keystone areas of technology that require further development and are essential to realizing these opportunities, as well as ongoing work to overcome these challenges.

Items.Authors: Gordon J. Stacey, POEMM Team
Items.Title: POEMM: the planetary origins and evolution multi-spectral monochromator
Items.Abstract: POEMM is a 1.8-meter balloon-borne telescope under development as a NASA Astrophysics Pioneers Mission. Leveraging new VIPA spectrometer and absorber-coupled MKID technologies POEMM promises unprecedented sensitivity at high spectral resolving power in the far-IR. POEMM is optimized to study the evolution of protoplanetary disks into planetary systems through velocity resolving low-lying HD and water vapor rotational transitions, and the 63 μm [OI] line which tomographically reveals the distribution of disk mass, the thermochemistry of cool water vapor, and the energy balance within disks as a function of radial distance from the central star, with sub-AU precision. POEMM's grating spectrometer will measure the largely unexplored solid-state water ice emission features at 43, 47, and 62 μm, measuring ice mass. POEMM will be launched from McMurdo during the Austral summer of 2029-2030. This presentation provides an overview of science, technology, instrument design and mission profile.

Items.Authors: Malcolm Smith, Edward Chapin, Dan Kerley, Jonathan Stocks, Jean-Pierre Véran, Alfio T. Puglisi
Items.Title: Results and lessons learned from MORFEO hard real-time controller prototyping results using HEART
Items.Abstract: The Herzberg Extensible Adaptive optics Real-Time Toolkit (HEART) is being developed after a decade of software design work on the NFIRAOS Real-Time Controller. HEART is being used as the RTC basis for several facility adaptive optics systems, including GNAO and GPI2 for the Gemini observatory and MORFEO and NFIRAOS for the ELT and TMT observatories, respectively.  Computer hardware has become much more powerful since the NFIRAOS RTC benchmarking of 2017. A single high performance CPU can now replace a quad socket server. This reduces hardware costs, power consumption and also software development costs.  In order to achieve good performance from these modern CPUs, an increased understanding of the architectural details is requires so that potential bottlenecks and sources of increased latency are avoided.  In this paper, we will discuss both the results of the prototyping performed during the MORFEO final design and also present our lessons learned which may help other developers.

Items.Authors: Claudia V. Rodrigues, Clemens D. Gneiding, Leandro Almeida, André L. Alves, Laerte B. Andrade, Denis V. Bernardes, Jesulino B. dos Santos, Julio C. Campagnolo, Fernando Falkenberg, Ana C. Mattiuci, Luciano Fraga, Francisco J. Jablonski, René Laporte, Eder Martioli, Flávio F. Ribeiro, Francisco Rodrigues, Juliano Romao, Wagner Schlindwein, Orlando Verducci, Gustavo H. Santos
Items.Title: SPARC4 - Simultaneous Polarimeter And Rapid Camera in 4 bands: a new instrument to Pico dos Dias Observatory
Items.Abstract: SPARC4 (Simultaneous Polarimeter And Rapid Camera in 4 bands) is a new facility instrument developed for the 1.6 m telescope at Pico dos Dias Observatory (OPD). This Brazilian initiative is the result of a joint effort between the National Institute for Space Research (INPE) and the National Laboratory for Astrophysics (LNA). Following its first light in November 2022 and comprehensive commissioning throughout 2023, the instrument is fully operational. Performance verification data demonstrate excellent optical quality, with both photometric and polarimetric modes delivering signal-to-noise ratios primarily limited by photon and detector noises. A dedicated Python-based data reduction pipeline has been released to support analysis. SPARC4 is available to the community as of the 2024A semester.

Items.Authors: Niyati Desai, Lorenzo König, Garreth J. Ruane, Susan F. Redmond, Jorge D. Llop-Sayson, A. J. Riggs
Items.Title: Testbed upgrades and strategies to improve contrast of the dimpled scalar vortex coronagraph
Items.Abstract: Scalar vortex coronagraphs (SVCs) are promising for future high-contrast imaging missions because they provide a true dual-polarization coronagraph solution. We present the first vacuum testbed demonstration of a SVC on the Decadal Survey Testbed 2 (DST2) at NASA’s High Contrast Imaging Testbed (HCIT), where the dimpled SVC achieved a mean contrast of 1.91×10⁻⁹ in 1% broadband light over a 3–10 λ/D half-sided dark hole. Motivated by this result, we pursued upgrades to the In-Air Coronagraph Testbed (IACT), where previous SVC demonstrations had been limited by a contrast floor near 10⁻⁸. Improvements included upgrading the broadband light source, reducing background light, and utilizing camera binning. These upgrades enabled a new in-air SVC contrast record of 5.11×10⁻⁹ in 1% broadband light over a 3–10 λ/D dark hole. Together, these results establish the first vacuum validation of a SVC and demonstrate a clear path toward advancing SVC technology for future HWO-level performance.

Items.Authors: David H. Hughes, F. Peter Schloerb, Min S. Yun, Grant W. Wilson, Kamal Souccar, José Luis Hernández Rebollar, Alfredo Montaña, David Omar Sánchez Argüelles, Arturo Gómez Ruiz, Iván Rodríguez Montoya, Gopal Narayanan, Alexandra Pope, Itziar Aretxaga, David M. Gale, Aldo Batta, Eric Emmanuel Martinez Garcia, Mark Heyer, Victor Hugo Gómez Rivera, José Ramón Valdés Parra, Raúl Naranjo Romero, Zhiyuan Ma
Items.Title: The Large Millimeter Telescope Alfonso Serrano (LMT): status, performance and upgrades
Items.Abstract: The Large Millimeter Telescope (LMT) Alfonso Serrano is a bi-national (Mexico and USA) telescope facility constructed on the summit of Sierra Negra, at an altitude of 4600m, in the Mexican state of Puebla. The LMT is a 50-m diameter single-dish radio-telescope designed, constructed and optimized to conduct scientific observations using heterodyne and continuum receivers, as well as VLBI observations, at frequencies between ~70 and 350 GHz. The LMT has an active surface control-system to correct gravitational and thermal deformations of the primary reflector to enable both night-time and daytime observations. We describe the current status and technical performance of the LMT, the instrumentation development program, and an on-going series of engineering and technical upgrades that will increase the optical efficiency and sensitivity of the telescope which will improve the overall scientific productivity and operational efficiency of the LMT.

Items.Authors: Jean-François Sauvage, Benoît Neichel, Lisa-Marie Mazzolo, Vincent Chambouleyron, Cédric Taïssir Héritier Salama, Thierry Fusco, Sylvain Oberti, Noah Schwartz, Bethany Johnson, Guido Agapito, Lorenzo Busoni, Jean-Pierre Véran, Timothy J. Morris, Anne Costille, David Le Mignant, Kjetil Dohlen, Calum Lithgow, William Taylor, James Dunlop
Items.Title: HARMONI at ELT: status of the HARMONI MCAO mode
Items.Abstract: HARMONI is the first light near-IR integral field spectrograph for the ELT. To achieve a large number of science cases, HARMONI will be equipped with three flavors of Adaptive Optics system, including a multi-conjugate (MCAO) mode; this is made possible by the recent coupling of the HARMONI instrument with the MCAO capability of the MORFEO instrument. We will present the Technical Specifications of this mode. We will demonstrate how its complements ELT AO capabilities in terms of AO performance and science. We model that the MCAO mode of HARMONI will provide better performance than the original LTAO mode in term of both achieved Strehl and sky coverage, providing margin to this wide field mode. The coupling with MORFEO has also been the opportunity of revisiting the contribution of NGS configurations, which will be detailed. We will also report on the architecture of the real-time control system, as well as the verification and validation approaches for this mode.

Items.Authors: Pradip R. Gatkine, Gregory Sercel, Nemanja Jovanovic, James Kent Wallace, Jeffrey Jewell, Dimitri Mawet
Items.Title: Developing high-efficiency high-resolution photonic spectrographs for astronomy
Items.Abstract: Astrophotonic spectrographs offer a unique capability to miniature astronomical spectrographs by several orders of magnitude and eliminate any moving parts by leveraging single-mode (i.e. diffraction-limited) input. Arrayed waveguide gratings is one of the most promising architectures for building high-resolution spectrographs.  To identify the most efficient material platforms, we constructed high-resolution spectrographs in two leading low-loss material platforms: Silicon nitride, and doped silica.   In particular, we build spectrograph chips with R ~ 12,000 and R ~ 26,000 using both material platforms in H-band (1400-1700 nm), both with a free spectral range of ~12 nm. We characterized these spectrographs over abroad band (1250-1650 nm) to compare their broadband efficiency and resolving power performance. Here, we present a comparison of the two material platforms at these high resolving powers. This paves the foundation for selecting an appropriate material platform for astronomy.

Items.Authors: Paolo Soffitta, Elisabetta Baracchini, Stefano Basso, Jörg Bayer, Benedikt Bergmann, Enrico Bozzo, Stefano Cesare, Enrico Costa, Elisabetta Costantini, Walter Cugno, Klaus Desch, Giorgio Dho, Sergio Fabiani, Davide Fiorina, Markus Gruber, Sebastien Guillot, Ian Hutchinson, Hemanth Manikantan, Jochen Kaminski, Irfan Kuvvetli, Alessandro Lacerenza, Carlo Lefevre, Fabio Muleri, Paul O'Brien, Giovanni Pareschi, Mark Pearce, Vladislavs Plesanovs, Stefano Piacentini, Alda Rubini, Ajay Ratheesh, Selina Ringsborg Howalt Owe, Daniele Spiga, Gianpiero Tagliaferri, Chris Tenzer, Berend Winter, Silvia Zane, Ivan Agudo, Lorenzo Amati, Stefano Bianchi, Niccolò Bucciantini, Carl Budtz-Jørgensen, Søren Krinstian Brandt, Jerome Chenevez, Martina Cardillo, Eugene Churazov, Enrico Costa, Stefano Covino, Alessandro Di Marco, Tiziana Di Salvo, Desiree Della Monica Ferreira, Michal Dovciak, Lorenzo Ducci, Hua Feng, Riccardo Ferrazzoli, Giancarlo Ghirlanda, Andrea Gnarini, Jeremy Heyl, Allan Hornstrup, Adam Ingram, Philip Kaaret, Ildar Khabibullin, Fabian Kislat, Henric Krawczynski, Yannis Liodakis, Liu Hooghui, Niels Lund, Frédéric Marin, Lorenzo Marra, Alan Marscher, Herman Marshall, Giorgio Matt, romana mikusincova, Alexander Mushtukov, Lara Nava, Alessandro Papitto, Pierre-olivier petrucci, Juri Poutanen, Agata Roszanska, Andrea Santangelo, Patrick Slane, James Steiner, Valery Suleimanov, Jiri Svoboda, Fabrizio Tavecchio, Roberto Taverna, Sergey Tsygankov, Youli Tuo, Roberto Turolla, Francesco Ursini, Alexandra Veledina, Jacco Vink, Martin Weisskopf
Items.Title: EXPO: a quantum leap in fast, wide-band X-ray polarimetry for astrophysics
Items.Abstract: The Enhanced X-ray Polarimetry Observatory (EXPO) is a proposed X-ray polarimetry mission submitted to ESA as the eighth Medium-Size mission candidate, with a prospective launch around 2041. EXPO passed the Step-1 down-selection. Selection for phase-0 is expected in September 2026. EXPO builds on and extends the capabilities of IXPE, pushing X-ray polarimetry into the hard X-ray band and introducing fast, Swift-like autonomous repointing. Its payload enables imaging photoelectric polarimetry up to 35 keV and non-imaging spectro-polarimetry up to 80 keV, with a suite of multilayer monolithic mirrors achieving 15″–30″ Half-Energy Width, depending on energy. The polarimetric telescopes are complemented by a Wide-Field Imager, a clone of ECLAIRs/SVOM, a Spectral-Imaging Camera, offering high-quality spectra, and the Instrument Control Unit managing the payload and the fast-repointing. This talk shows its characteristics and illustrates how EXPO overcomes the principal limitations of IXPE.

Items.Authors: Edward L. Chapin, Kate Jackson, Dan Kerley, Malcolm Smith, Jonathan Stocks, Maaike van Kooten, Jean-Pierre Véran
Items.Title: HEART: soft real-time control system architecture for adaptive optics
Items.Abstract: The control systems for several facility-class adaptive optics systems at observatories including Gemini, TMT and the ELT, are currently being constructed using the Herzberg Extensible Adaptive optics Real-Time Toolkit (HEART). This paper covers the design of the soft real-time (SRT) components of these systems that use statistics generated by the hard real-time (HRT) control system to perform parameter optimizations. The SRT is written predominantly in Python to make it more accessible to adaptive optics scientists who may wish to experiment with different algorithms. Depending on the observatory and interface requirements, different mechanisms may be required for I/O. We also discuss how we deal with synchronization issues in larger AO systems for which the control system is distributed across multiple physical servers.

Items.Authors: Yoo Jung Kim, Michael Fitzgerald, Sebastien Vievard, Jonathan Lin, Yinzi Xin, Miles Lucas, Olivier Guyon, Julien Lozi, Vincent Deo, Elsa Huby, Sylvestre Lacour, Manon Lallement, Aidan Walk, Sanny Ahmed, Rodrigo Amezcua-Correa, Pradip Gatkine, Harry-Dean Kenchington Goldsmith, Sergio Leon-Saval, Barnaby Norris, Mathias Nowak, Anusha Pai Asnodkar, Steph Sallum, Jehanne Sarrazin, Adam Taras, Stephanos Yerolatsitis, Nemanja Jovanovic
Items.Title: Photonic lanterns for high-angular-resolution astronomy: on-sky demonstration and the path to higher-contrast mode-based imaging
Items.Abstract: Diffraction limits the angular resolution achievable by direct imaging. Spatial-mode-based imaging, which measures light in a modal basis, can achieve subdiffraction resolution by preserving phase information. We demonstrate this capability on-sky using a 19-port photonic lantern (PL)-fed spectrometer at the Subaru Telescope (FIRST-PL), achieving 50 μas Hα spectroastrometric precision and revealing disk asymmetry around β CMi. Additional tests with a 3-port PL demonstrate the technique’s robustness with fewer-mode devices. While successful, using a PL alone, which sorts modes on a fixed basis, is sub-optimal for high-contrast observations. We address this limitation by feeding mode-selective PL outputs into an active photonic integrated circuit (PIC), enabling real-time reconfiguration of the measurement basis and simultaneous wavefront sensing. Numerical simulations and initial laboratory results demonstrate the concept, establishing a path toward a configurable mode-based imager.

Items.Authors: Karwan Rostem, Gordon J. Stacey
Items.Title: POEMM: an overview of the design and performance expectation of the science instrument element
Items.Abstract: The Planetary Origins and Evolution Multispectral Monochromator (POEMM) is a 1.8-meter balloon-borne far-infrared telescope recently selected as a NASA Astrophysics Pioneers Mission. POEMM is designed to directly probe the evolution of protoplanetary disks. The POEMM science instrument element (SIE) has three spectrometer modules: (i) HR1 is designed to achieve velocity-resolved measurements of the HD J=1-0 emission at 112µm with R~100,000; (ii) HR2 will selectively observe four spectral lines at R~50,000: two water vapor transitions at 40.69 and 46.48 µm, the HD J=2-1 line at 56.23 µm and the [OI] 63.18 µm line; (iii) LR, a grating spectrometer, will cover 35-70 µm and the important broadband water-ice features at 43 and 63 µm. In this presentation, we provide an overview of the SIE cryostat design, spectrometer modules, optical layout, and expected sensitivity. POEMM is scheduled for launch in the Austral 2029-2030 summer.

Items.Authors: Alan M. Watson, Noémie Globus
Items.Title: TEQUILA: Mechanism-free polarimetry for astronomy
Items.Abstract: TEQUILA is a new imaging photopolarimeter developed for the COLIBRÍ telescope, a 1.3-meter rapid-response facility designed for transient science and located at the Observatorio Astronómico Nacional, Mexico. The instrument employs Sony’s Polarsens CMOS technology, which integrates wire-grid micro-polarizers directly above the detector pixels at four fixed orientations. This architecture enables simultaneous, single-exposure measurement of the linear Stokes parameters (Q, U, I) without rotating optics or other mechanical modulation systems. TEQUILA is also optimized for rapid transient follow-up, allowing observations of gamma-ray burst afterglows and other optical transients within one minute of an alert. This capability provides a practical and robust platform for real-time polarimetric monitoring and represents a pathfinder for future low-cost, mechanism-free polarimetric instruments. In this paper, we describe the design of TEQUILA and our experience with it on-sky.

Items.Authors: Fernando Quirós-Pacheco, Cédric Plantet, Bo Xin, Arielle Bertrou-Cantou, Jordi Molgo, Paulo Henrique Silva, Nicolò Azzaroli, Juan Pablo Haddad, Gary Muller, Alfio Puglisi, Fabio Rossi, Diogo Slepetys, Josema Filgueira, Aline Souza, Dana Adams, Brian McLeod, Jan Kansky, Daniel Catropa, Simone Esposito, Richard Demers
Items.Title: The GMT Adaptive optics and Phasing Sensors testbed (GAPS): status report of coarse and fine phasing experiments with the natural guide star wavefront sensor prototype of the Giant Magellan Telescope
Items.Abstract: The GMT Adaptive optics and Phasing Sensors testbed (GAPS) is one of the key risk reduction projects that GMTO is performing under a National Science Foundation (NSF) sponsored award, to validate key optical control aspects of the GMT Natural Guide star Adaptive Optics (NGAO) mode, including coarse phasing with an Holographic Dispersed Fringe Sensor, and fine phasing control with a Pyramid WFS under realistic observing conditions.    GAPS integrates a prototype of the dual-channel Natural Guide star Wavefront Sensor (NGWS) with a GMT telescope simulator reproducing the GMT pupil geometry with seven segments actuated in piston, tip, and tilt (PTT). A 2k Deformable Mirror (DM) is used as a proxy for the GMT Adaptive Secondary Mirror (ASM) on the testbed.    We report in this paper the results of laboratory experiments demonstrating coarse and fine phasing control under the presence of various turbulence strengths and illumination levels.

Items.Authors: Saraswathi Kalyani Subramanian, Kyle Van Gorkom, Ramya Anche, Kian Milani, Jaren Ashcraft, Heejoo Choi, Kevin Derby, Olivier Durney, Daewook Kim, Irina Stefan, Ewan Douglas
Items.Title: The Space Coronagraph Optical Bench (SCoOB): 10. dark zone maintenance for space-based high contrast imaging testbed
Items.Abstract: The detection and characterization of Earth-like exoplanets is one of the key scientific goals of future space observatories. Achieving this requires starlight suppression at contrasts of the order of 10-10. Maintaining these contrasts over long integration times is essential to image faint planets. In practice, this is challenging due to the mechanical instabilities and thermal gradients within the telescope that give rise to quasi-static wavefront errors. Dark Zone Maintenance (DZM) techniques can mitigate these effects by stabilizing the wavefront in realtime. We present the results from simulations of an extended Kalman filter (EKF)-based DZM algorithm implemented on a model of SCoOB (a vector vortex coronagraph with a charge-6 vector vortex wave plate and Kilo-C DM) to maintain the contrast at ~10-8 within a one-sided dark hole from 3–10 lambda/D in the presence of injected drifts and the latest results from the testbed.

Items.Authors: Fabio Muleri, Luca Baldini, Sudip Chakraborty, Chien-Ting Chen, Enrico Costa, Ettore Del Monte, Alessandro Di Marco, Kurtis L. Dietz, Sergio Fabiani, Riccardo Ferrazzoli, Philip Kaaret, Alberto Manfreda, Stephen L. O'Dell, John Rankin, Brian D. Ramsey, Carmelo Sgrò, Paolo Soffitta, Douglas A. Swartz, Allyn F. Tennant, Alessio Trois, Martin C. Weisskopf
Items.Title: In-orbit anomaly and recovery of IXPE detector 2
Items.Abstract: The Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer (IXPE) is a NASA-ASI mission launched in December 2021 and dedicated to the measurement of linear polarization in the X-ray energy range, between 2 and 8 keV. The payload is comprised of three identical telescopes, with grazing-incidence mirrors focusing radiation on focal plane photoelectric polarimeters based on the Gas Pixel Detector design. On 14 April 2025, the second detector had an anomaly that changed significantly the electrical behaviour of the ASIC which reads out the image of the photoelectron tracks. In this contribution, we describe the effect of the anomaly on the instrumental response and the actions taken to mitigate its effects and recover the scientific observations of the instrument.

Items.Authors: Christina Vides, Steph Sallum, Andy Skemer, Ruth Murray-Clay, Josh Eisner
Items.Title: The search for protoplanets with aperture masking: new constraints on disk architectures and the underlying protoplanet population
Items.Abstract: Protoplanetary disks serve as natural planet formation laboratories. Interferometric techniques, such as non-redundant masking (NRM), allow for the characterization of gas giant accretion timescales and dynamical interactions by imaging protoplanetary disks with tracers of forming planets. With NRM, we can achieve angular resolution down to and within the diffraction limit, and image planet formation on solar system scales. We present the results of a NIRC2 NRM survey with a sample of 30 protoplanetary disks. From this survey, we obtain long time baseline observations of a protoplanet candidate and characterize disk structure in several targets. We map the protoplanet detection probabilities for each target and the survey as a whole using mass-times-accretion rate sensitivities. From these results, we place statistical constraints on the underlying protoplanet population and the timescales of gas giant accretion at spatial separations down to ~7 AU.

Items.Authors: Wei Wang, Meng Zhai, Gang Zhao, Jifeng Liu, Boqian Xu, Xuejun Zhang, Jin Chang
Items.Title: Tianlin: a 6.6m UV/VIS/NIR space telescope dedicated to the search for exolife evidence
Items.Abstract: The ongoing and upcoming space-based planet survey missions, such as TESS, PLATO, and ET, are expected to discover thousands of small- to medium-sized planets, including over 100 potentially habitable rocky planets. To further study these Earth 2.0, the exoplanetary science community has proposed various follow-up missions. However, none of these missions will be able to characterize the atmospheres of Earth-like planets in habitable zones or detect potential biosignatures. China is pushing Tianlin, a 6.6m UV-to-NIR space telescope, projected to begin operations around 2035+ with a mission lifespan exceeding 10 years. Tianlin's primary goal will be to characterize rocky planets in the habitable zones of nearby stars, with a focus on identifying potential biosignatures. Additionally, this mission aims to significantly enhance our understanding of exoplanet populations, nearby galaxies, and the early universe. International collaborations in multiple disciplines are welcome.

Items.Authors: Renzo Ramelli, Andrea F. Battaglia, Franziska Zeuner, Svetlana Berdyugina, Michele Bianda, Francesco Vitali, Daniele Allegri, Roberto Gardenghi, Marco Rogantini, Giuseppe Di Dato, Luca N. Bezzola
Items.Title: Recent developments in high precision solar spectro-polarimetry with the ZIMPOL imaging polarimeter
Items.Abstract: The Zurich imaging polarimeter (ZIMPOL) allows to perform full Stokes solar spectro-polarimetry with a precision down to 10 ppm by applying a fast modulation and a special on-chip demodulation technique, suppressing seeing induced cross-talks. ZIMPOL is employed routinely at the Gregory Coudé Telescope at the IRSOL observatory and in dedicated solar observing campaign at the GREGOR Telescope in Tenerife. We present the recent developments of the ZIMPOL system. In particular we are recently commissioning a new version with a redesigned electronics that allows to improve the efficiency of the system by drastically reducing the overhead times. In addition, by combining fast modulation with a slow rotating retarder, it has been possible to develop an observing technique that suppresses systematic errors and permit to achieve a polarimetric accuracy down to 10^-5.

Items.Authors: Zeyu Deng, Shijie Ke, Zhangqi Dang, Jian Ge, Ziyang Zhang
Items.Title: Adaptive optics in waveguide: conversion from arbitrary multimode to single-mode
Items.Abstract: A waveguide-based adaptive optics device is developed utilizing a 3D multimode waveguide with multilayer electrodes attached. We name this device the Mode Detangler (MD). The MD device exhibits the capability to transform arbitrary inputs from multimode fibers into single-mode-like spots through a real-time optimization algorithm, thereby enabling seamless coupling with single-mode fibers. Compared with direct multimode-to-single-mode fiber coupling, the mode detangler device provides a transmission improvement exceeding 15 dB. Furthermore, the MD obtains a total insertion loss (encompassing bidirectional coupling losses and propagation loss) of less than 5 dB across a broad spectral range, spanning from the visible band (635 nm) to the near-infrared band (1550 nm).

Items.Authors: Carlos M. Correia, Maud Langlois, Markus Kasper, Adam Taras, Anna Rahim, Anthony Boccaletti, Arnaud Sevin, Aurélie Magniez, Camille Graf, Caroline Kulcsar, Charlotte Bond, Damien Gratadour, Emiliano Doolaiti, Fausto Cortecchia, Florian Ferreira, Gianluca Di Rico, Gilles Orban de Xivry, Henri-François Raynaud, Jalo Nousiainen, Laura Schreiber, Louis Desdoigts, Mamadou N'Diaye, Manal Chebbo, Markus Feldt, Matteo Lombini, Michel Tallon, Miska Le Louarn, Nicolas Galland, Noah Schwartz, Pierre Vermot, Rico Landman, Runa Briguglio, Sebastiaan Haffert, Thomas Bertram, Tim Morris, Valentin Fonteneau, Vincent Chambouleyron
Items.Title: Closing the technology gap for the Extremely Large Telescope’s Planetary Camera and Spectrograph (ELT-PCS): its extreme adaptive optics system conceptual design
Items.Abstract: We provide the results of a trade-off analysis using comparative simulations of a two-stage sequential cascaded control loop featuring two wavefront sensors and two deformable mirrors versus a single wavefront sensor splitting correction amongst two mirrors in a woofer-tweeter configuration for the extreme adaptive optics system of the future ELT Planetary Camera and Spectrograph

Items.Authors: Jenna Samra, Alan Hsu, Vanessa Marquez, Aaron Oppenheimer, Ryan Chaves, Peter Cheimets, Edward DeLuca, Giulio Del Zanna, Gabriel Dubinsky, Daniel Durusky, Mark Freeman, Leon Golub, Jacob Hawthorne, Vladimir Kradinov, Maxim Kramar, Hannah Levin, Haosheng Lin, Kyle MacKenzie, Chad Madsen, Cem Onyuksel, Hannah Rana, Patrick Rohleder, Andrew Schalk, Paola Testa, Steven Tomczyk, Edward Udinski, Abigail Unger, Patrick Zmarzly
Items.Title: A balloon-borne infrared coronagraph and spectropolarimeter for magnetic field measurements of the solar corona
Items.Abstract: The Coronal Spectropolarimeter for Airborne Infrared Research (CORSAIR) is a balloon-borne infrared coronagraph and spectropolarimeter funded by NASA’s Heliophysics Low Cost Access to Space (H-LCAS) program and currently under development at Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory (SAO). CORSAIR will make global, long-duration measurements of temperature, density, velocity and magnetic field in the solar corona by measuring the polarization state of five emission lines with wavelengths from 1 to 4 microns. The project incorporates various engineering challenges associated with making high-resolution, high-sensitivity observations spanning two octaves in wavelength in a low-cost package on a balloon-borne platform. CORSAIR is currently undergoing integration, alignment, testing, and calibration in preparation for its qualification flight in late summer 2026. In this paper, we describe the scientific goals, instrument design, ongoing integration, and plans for the qualification flight.

Items.Authors: Alan J. Kogut, Hugo Bourque, Matthew Buchan, Eric Carbonneau, Alain Cournoyer, Dale Fixsen, Jonathan Papa, Robert Podgurski, Lenward Seals
Items.Title: Design and operation of the PRIMA Fourier transform module
Items.Abstract: The Probe far-Infrared Mission for Astrophysics (PRIMA) is a mission concept under development for NASA's Astrophysics Probe Explorer Program. The FIRESS instrument couples light from a cryogenic 1.8-meter telescope through a Martin-Puplett interferometer and onto four long-slit grating spectrometers. The resulting post-dispersion Fourier transform achieves background-limited sensitivity with resolving power R = 4400 x (112 microns / lambda) at far-infrared wavelengths lambda = 24--235microns. We describe the optical design and calibration of the Fourier transform module, the reconstruction of sky spectra from the sampled interferograms, and the projected instrument performance.

Items.Authors: Charlotte Z. Bond, Jean-François Sauvage, David Barr, Sylvain Cetre, Alexis Carlotti, Noah Schwartz, Timothy Morris, Romain Fétick, Cédric Taïssir Héritier, Ben Buky, Arnaud Striffling, Matteo Pasinetti, Vincent Chambouleyron, Angelie Alagao, Kjetil Dohlen, Benoît Neichel, Thierry Fusco
Items.Title: HARMONI at ELT: from simulations to on-sky prototyping of the HARMONI single conjugate AO system
Items.Abstract: HARMONI is the first light, adaptive optics assisted, near-IR integral field spectrograph for the ELT. It can operate in two adaptive optics modes - SCAO (including a high contrast capability) and MCAO. The SCAO system for HARMONI is based on a pyramid wavefront sensor operating between 700 and 1000 nm. Here we present an overview of the SCAO performance, including an analysis of the secondary loops required for high contrast operation.   We report on prototyping of the SCAO real-time controller deployed on the PAPYRUS AO testbed, validating the real time processing pipeline on-sky. We present the first on-sky demonstration of the HARMONI approach to optical gain tracking and compensation, based on AO telemetry, and compare with a direct measurement approach using a focal plane camera. Finally, we demonstrate tracking of environmental parameters (r0, windspeed etc.) and their use in the optimisation of the AO loop.

Items.Authors: Roland H. den Hartog, Phil Uttley, Angela Di Virgilio, Adrian Martindale, Thomas Buggey, Luc Voruz
Items.Title: Introducing XRIstel: the X-ray interferometric space telescope
Items.Abstract: X-ray interferometry has the potential to revolutionize astronomy with a 10000 times higher spatial resolution (below 100 micro-arcsec) than current X-ray observatories. With spectro-astrometry techniques scales below 1 micro-arcsec may be probed. Potential science cases range from exo-planets, to X-ray binaries, nearby SMBHs and more distant AGN coronae. Although X-ray interferometric space missions have been studied in the past, never before has the technological landscape been more inviting to endeavor such a project. In this paper we describe how XRIstel, a European X-ray Interferometric Space Telescope is taking shape thanks to a series of remarkable technological advances. In this paper we will discuss both the fascinating window on the Universe that XRIstel will open, and the technological breakthroughs that make it feasible.

Items.Authors: Guillermo Martin, Manon Lallement, Elsa Huby, Sylvestre Lacour, Ciro d'Amico, Razvan Stoian, Sebastien Vievard, Olivier Guyon, Jehanne Sarrazin, Guodong Zhang, Guanghua Cheng
Items.Title: Novel interferometric beam combiners for multi-T instruments in the visible and near IR
Items.Abstract: In this work, we focus on the design, fabrication and characterization of two different types of photonic circuits: On one hand, we have developed 2D, classical photo-lithographic chips, using Ag:diffusion in glass, to achieve high contrast, sharp bending radii, single-mode waveguides in the Visible. The fabricated chip is a 5T beam combiner, devoted to FIRST/SUBARU instrument. We will present the interferometric performances of these 2D PICs when exposed to a point-like light source (single star) or a two-points-like light source (binary) on the FIRST/SUBARU instrument replica built at LIRA – Observatoire de Paris.   On the other hand, we have developed 3D 5T laser-written chips, to reduce crosstalk observed in planar PICs, and therefore increase the instrument’s stability and sensitivity. In this second part of the work, tests on transmission, polarization behavior and fringe contrast will be presented.

Items.Authors: Saikrishna Manojkumar, Susan F. Redmond, Leonid Pogorelyuk, Christine L. Page, Garreth J. Ruane, Niyati Desai, Kerri L. Cahoy
Items.Title: Broadband focal plane modal estimation of high-order wavefront drifts on coronagraphic testbeds
Items.Abstract: The Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) aims to directly image Exo-Earths 10 orders of magnitude dimmer than their host star. Algorithms such as dark zone maintenance (DZM) have been proposed to mitigate high-order wavefront drifts and maintain contrast. A modal dark zone maintenance (MDZM) approach, which represents and corrects drifting wavefronts in the deformable mirror (DM) actuator basis, has demonstrated improvement in closed-loop contrast performance by a factor of 5 in simulation in 2.5 in hardware. However, these results were confined to narrowband estimation and control. This work expands the MDZM formulation to use broadband images in simulation using the Decadal Survey Testbed (DST) simulator FALCO and in hardware using the In-Air Coronagraph Testbed (IACT) at NASA JPL. The resulting contrast performance is compared to traditional broadband DZM, as well as narrowband DZM and MDZM, across various drift rates and signal-to-noise ratios inside the dark zone of the speckles.

Items.Authors: Luca Castaldini, Andrea Bulgarelli, Nicolò Parmiggiani, Adriano De Rosa, Alessio Aboudan, Lorenzo Amati, Andrea Argan, Paolo Calabretto, Francescopiero Calzolari, Riccardo Campana, Ambra Di Piano, Francesca Esposito, Riccardo Falco, Antonio Femia, Fabrizio Fiore, Valentina Fioretti, Ezequiel Joaquin Marchesini, Angela Marinoni, Mattia Maniscalco, Eduardo Medinaceli Villegas, Ghulam Mustafa, Gabriele Panebianco, Alessandro Rizzo, Luca Spadoni, Alessio Trois, Enrico Virgilli, Luca Zarri
Items.Title: GammaSky: real-time edge processing for high-energy events
Items.Abstract: GammaSky pathfinder is a project developing edge Artificial Intelligence computing solutions for real-time acquisition and processing of X- and gamma-ray phenomena such as Terrestrial Gamma-ray Flashes. Building on the heritage of ASI/AGILE and the Gamma-Flash project, it explores onboard processing strategies relevant to future space missions. The system is deployed at the “O. Vittori” Observatory on Monte Cimone, Italy and integrates a Luxium SiPM scintillation detector with a RedPitaya STEMlab 125-14 for high-rate, GPS-tagged waveform acquisition. Data are processed on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano using classical reconstruction and AI-based methods, supported by a modular C++ Real-Time Analysis Data Processor framework. GammaSky provides a realistic testbed for advanced edge processing, with developments that may benefit upcoming initiatives such as the PRORIS program. We present the latest updates on the Gammasky system design and implementation.

Items.Authors: Álvaro González, Philip R. Jewell, Elizabeth Humphreys, Martin A. Zwaan, Misato Fukagawa, George Kosugi, Norikazu Mizuno, John Carpenter, Sean M. Dougherty
Items.Title: The ALMA wideband sensitivity upgrade: 2026 status report
Items.Abstract: ALMA, the world’s premier ground-based facility for (sub)millimeter astronomy, has been producing transformative science since beginning operations in 2011. The Wideband Sensitivity Upgrade (WSU) is the top-priority initiative for the ALMA Development Roadmap, released in 2018 to prioritize the developments necessary to significantly expand ALMA’s capabilities and enhance its scientific reach in the coming decades. This contribution will provide a status update of the WSU Program planning and implementation.

Items.Authors: Abani S. Nayak, Julius Göhring, Martin M. Roth, Kalaga V. Madhav
Items.Title: All-Fiber Broadband Wavelength-Division Multiplexing using Heterogeneous Photonic Lanterns
Items.Abstract: This work introduces an all-fiber broadband wavelength-division multiplexing architecture utilizing 1×7 heterogeneous photonic lanterns (PLs), specifically PL-(6+1) and PL-(4+3). By combining mismatched single-mode cores, such as SM450 and SMF28, the devices enable passive, wavelength-selective spatial routing. Experimental results show distinct dual-regime performance: in the visible band (350--740 nm), they act as multi-channel broadband collectors, while in the H-band (1520--1610 nm), core asymmetries break mode degeneracy, thereby enabling passive spectral sorting. These findings highlight the potential of heterogeneous fiber bundles for next-generation astronomical facilities that require simultaneous multi-wavelength capabilities to feed separate, band-optimized spectrographs.

Items.Authors: Eden A. McEwen, Jared R. Males, Olivier Guyon, Sebastiaan Y. Haffert, Joseph D. Long, Logan Pearce, Laird M. Close, Warren B. Foster, Kyle Van Gorkom, Alex D. Hedglen, Parker T. Johnson, Maggie Y. Kautz, Jay K. Kueny, Jialin Li, Joshua Liberman, Miles Lucas, Jennifer Lumbres, Avalon L. McLeod, Lauren Schatz, Elena Tonucci, Katie Twitchell, Alycia Weinberger
Items.Title: Comparing real-time optical gain measurement and methods on MagAO-X
Items.Abstract: A lingering technical challenge for pyramid wavefront sensors (PyWFS) is their change in response between calibration and correction residuals, a quantity known as optical gain (OG). Given the prevalence of PyWFSs in high-contrast adaptive optics systems (AO), understanding and reliably measuring OG for real time control unlocks advanced correction and post processing techniques. This work compares optical gain measurement techniques on MagAO-X, a visible light (0.5-1.1 µm) extreme AO instrument on the 6.5m Magellan Clay telescope. We present a set of on-sky measurements of OG across three techniques. Throughout all measurements, we identify a relationship with variation in AO performance that follows seeing, and find on-sky OG approximately flat vs mode index. We compare these on-sky results against simulations fed by telemetry or AO system parameters. These simulations allow us to investigate how instrument design and atmospheric properties affect OG.

Items.Authors: Shaul Hanany, Kosuke Aizawa, Rex Lam, Scott Chapman, Scott Cray, Sam Dietterich, Calvin Firth, Takumi Izawa, Jürgen Koch, Tomotake Matsumura, Ryota Takaku
Items.Title: Alumina filter with subwavelength structure anti-reflection coating for the 800-900 GHz band of the CCAT Observatory’s Prime-Cam instrument
Items.Abstract: We present design, fabrication, and measurements of a prototype alumina filter for the CCAT Prime-Cam instrument 800-900 GHz band. CCAT's final 400 mm diameter filter is required to have an in-band transmission higher than 90%. The average reflectance loss of 43% anticipated with a sample without anti-reflection coating (ARC) is reduced to less than 5% by means of pyramid-like subwavelength structures (SWS) that have 95 micrometer pitch and up to 150 micrometer height. We fabricated the SWS-ARC on a 5 cm diameter sample using laser ablation. We report the measured transmittance and reflectance and discuss plans to extend the fabrication to the final 400 mm diameter. This is the first report of an alumina-based optical element with SWS-ARC at these high frequencies.

Items.Authors: Rob G. van Holstein, Suman Bhattacharyya, Marie Rodríguez, Christian Ginski, Sebastiaan Y. Haffert, Ryo Tazaki, Zahed Wahhaj
Items.Title: Combining long-slit spectroscopy and accurate polarimetry with SPHERE-IRDIS to characterize circumstellar disks
Items.Abstract: Dust and water ice in circumstellar disks can be studied with VLT/SPHERE-IRDIS’ near-infrared long-slit spectroscopy (LSS) mode, but previous attempts to extract disk spectra were hindered by strong contamination from stellar speckles. We devised an observation scheme that combines IRDIS LSS with polarimetry, creating the first high-contrast long-slit spectropolarimetric mode. Because direct starlight is essentially unpolarized, polarimetry strongly suppresses the stellar speckles, thereby revealing the disk spectrum. To validate the mode, we observed the bright planet-forming disk around HD 142527. After applying our data-reduction pipeline and correcting for instrumental polarization using a fully calibrated Mueller matrix model, we clearly recover the polarized spectra of the disk rings. The new mode enables the polarimetric characterization of dust properties and opens the way for the detection of water ice at angular separations smaller than those reachable with JWST.

Items.Authors: Aditya Garde, Roland den Hartog, Matthijs Langelaar, Henk Hoevers, Just Herder, Luc Voruz, Adam Lassise, Christian Körnig, Kevin Ravensberg, Nathan Ooijevaar, Phil Uttley
Items.Title: Design and development of an x-ray interferometry testbed
Items.Abstract: X-ray Interferometry(XRI) has the potential for ultra-high resolution imaging. The XRI design by Willingale allows the interferometer to be compact enough to fit in a single spacecraft. The approach has been tested in visible wavelength however, is yet to be tested with X-rays. Here we report on the design and the current status of the XRI testbed. We are currently building an facility at SRON to test the Willingale XRI. The facility will allow testing of a 1cm baseline XRI at 1.25keV. The testbed consists a rotating anode X-ray source. A slit mechanism is placed in front to have a spatially coherent beam. Further, it has a 15m long vacuum line including a vacuum chamber which houses an optical bench to mount the optics. The optics consists 3 flat mirrors and a slatted mirror fabricated by cosine. Mirrors are placed at grazing incidence with alignment mechanisms. The fringes will be detected by a CMOS. The development will serve as a platform for testing current and future XRI designs.

Items.Authors: Melissa L. Graham, Leanne P. Guy, Jeffrey L. Carlin, Christina L. Adair, Yumi Choi, Gloria Fonseca Alvarez, Shenming Fu, Sarah Greenstreet, Greg Madejski, Garreth Martin, Andrés A. Plazas Malagón, Aaron M. Meisner, James Edward Robinson, Douglas L. Tucker, Christina C. Williams, Jonathan Sick, Frossie Economou
Items.Title: Rubin Observatory's approach to providing sustainable scientific user support at scale
Items.Abstract: The data products from Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) are expected to be accessed and analyzed by ten thousand scientists and students worldwide. Supporting this large and diverse community to access the novel LSST data set requires an innovative and proactive community science model. This talk will provide an overview of the Rubin Observatory’s community science model, including policies, guidelines, and workflows for documentation, tutorials, activities, user support, and issue resolution. An evaluation of the model’s current implementation and how these components are working “in the wild”, with an eye towards the challenges of scaling up while maintaining inclusion and access and deriving metrics for scientific performance, will also be included.

Items.Authors: Christian Marois
Items.Title: Habitable Worlds Observatory: toward 10^10 contrast exoplanet detection/biomarker identification using a multi-band imaging Fourier transform spectrograph
Items.Abstract: The Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) aims to directly detect nearby earth-like exoplanets and search their atmospheres for biomarkers, requiring starlight suppression at 10^10 contrast over ~20% bandpasses—a major technical challenge. Even with an ultra-stable 6–8 m telescope, advanced coronagraphs, and extreme wavefront control, raw contrast alone is unlikely to meet these requirements for long-duration integrations. HWO will therefore depend on continuous focal-plane wavefront sensing to maintain a deep dark hole and post-processing while minimizing detector noise impacts.  I will present a Canadian imager concept optimized for sensitivity and biomarker characterization, compatible with current space-qualified visible detectors and emerging detector technologies. The instrument supports high-SNR focal-plane wavefront sensing/control and is designed to enhance final contrast with post-processing methods.

Items.Authors: Lucas Labadie, Kalaga Madhav, Robert J. Harris, Aline Dinkelaker, Kevin Barjot, Aurélien Benoît, Nicholas Scott, Sajjad Mahdizadeh, Viktoria Kutnohorsky, Ariadna Calcines Rosario, Joshua J. Guy, Emily Ronson, Robert R. Thomson, Tarun Sharma, Narsireddy Anugu, Alyssa V. Mayer, Gail Schaefer
Items.Title: NAIR-APREXIS: enabling photonics-based instruments for long-baseline interferometry and integral-field spectroscopy
Items.Abstract: In the NAIR collaboration, we aim to advance the development, integration, and operation of cutting-edge photonic instruments for infrared long-baseline interferometry and precision spectroscopy. We developed a single-mode integrated-optics astronomical K-band beam combiner, which we successfully tested on-sky using a single baseline of the CHARA Array. Across several observing campaigns, the prototype exhibited excellent stability, achieving 1% precision on the interferometric visibilities and a total throughput of 40%. We are also developing an integral field unit (IFU) is designed for exoplanet detection and characterisation, which is due to be tested with MagAO-X in Chile in 2026. We discuss our work to develop the next generation of astrophotonic technologies, including TPP micro-dispersers designed for low resolving power, high transmission applications. These results pave the way for future upgrades to astronomical instruments.

Items.Authors: Mohammad N. Islam, Xuan Du, Sean Heakes, Timothy Robishaw, Mehak Parihar
Items.Title: Performance modelling for radio telescopes: an integrated framework of metrology, finite element analysis and electromagnetic simulation
Items.Abstract: This paper introduces an integrated framework that merges finite element analysis, drone-based photogrammetry, and electromagnetic simulation to model radio telescope performance more accurately. Applied to the 26‑m John A. Galt Telescope, verified FEA models predict structural deformation from gravity and temperature, while drone-based photogrammetry measures surface deviations and feed misalignments and add ground references. These real-world data are used in electromagnetic simulation to evaluate beam shape and polarization changes at various positions. The workflow supports structurally informed optimization and enhances telescope precision and reliability

Items.Authors: Gioia Rau
Items.Title: Space and lunar interferometry: emerging concepts and pathways
Items.Abstract: Space and lunar interferometry are moving from long-range aspiration to a concrete landscape of mission studies, pathfinders, and staged architectures. This invited review surveys the field's principal pathways: free-flying interferometers, lunar-surface arrays, and hybrid space-VLBI. Mid-infrared nulling targets the thermal emission of temperate exoplanets; low-frequency radio arrays on the lunar far side open the low-frequency Universe from the only radio-quiet site in the inner Solar System; lunar UV/optical arrays aim to resolve the surfaces and magnetic activity of stars; far-infrared, space-VLBI, and X-ray concepts extend the reach to planet formation and black-hole physics; and lunar laser interferometry applies the lunar platform to mid-band gravitational waves. I map the enabling technologies these pathways share, and close with the key decisions, pathfinder sequencing, and funding models that can turn complementary concepts into operational observatories within the decade.

Items.Authors: Nicolás Rodríguez-Linares, Luzma Montoya, Yolanda Martín, Noelia Feijóo, Esther Soria, Javier León-Gil, Adrián Calzadilla, Miguel Núñez-Cagigal, Jorge Quintero-Nehrkorn
Items.Title: Status of the European Solar Telescope adaptive optics: simulation and bench results
Items.Abstract: The European Solar Telescope (EST) has completed the Preliminary Design Review (PDR) of its Single Conjugate Adaptive Optics (SCAO) system and real-time controller. We present an overview of the expected SCAO performance based on the consolidated preliminary design, including simulations of a dual-branch configuration at 500 nm and 680nm. The results, obtained with the new open-source Solar Adaptive Optics Simulator (SAOS) and validated against DASP, also evaluate key error sources specific to solar observations.  We summarise the performance of the proposed real-time controller, the Durham Adaptive Optics (DAO) platform, and the successful demonstration tests conducted with SAOS.

Items.Authors: Frossie Economou, Gregory P. Dubois-Felsmann, Russ Allbery, Stelios Voutsinas, Angelo Fausti Neto, Adam Thornton, Dan C. Fuchs, Jonathan Sick
Items.Title: The few-servers many-clients myth: lessons from the Rubin Science Platform
Items.Abstract: There is a sometimes unexamined belief that astronomical data services follow the general client server pattern found in general IT: for example there are relatively few HTTP server implementations but many browsers; there are relatively few IMAP implementations but a myriad of mail clients, etc. However even in the relatively recent past, this has not been the case for astronomical client-servers. For example, TOPCAT is the giant in the TAP client space, whereas every astronomical archive seems to have its own TAP server implementation.     This reverse asymmetry is even more evident with an environment such as the Rubin Science Platform. The argument can be made that in a science platform the users interact with a rather limited set of clients (pyvo in JupyterNotebooks or external APIs, perhaps a web portal based on Firefly or Aladin Lite), but to support that we have found dozens of server-side applications have to be written.    In this talk we will cover our anticipated im

Items.Authors: Giorgio Savini, Peter A.R. Ade, Peter Hargrave, Alexey Shitvov, Carole Tucker, Giampaolo Pisano, Jin Zhang
Items.Title: A novel metamaterial telescope technology for broadband mm-wave refractive observations
Items.Abstract: In this paper we present a novel metamaterial telescope composed exclusively of thin, flat elements, each being a tested hot-pressed photo-lithographic structure combining the properties of a lens, tuned anti-reflection and frequency selection or filtering.   We discuss the design process from ab-initio physical metamaterial properties of the single periodic cell structure to the  lens concept which constitutes the building block of the telescope design and the iterative process that is part of the lens optimization.   We discuss the results of a testing campaign using the single lens elements for different telescope designs showing on- and off-axis performance.

Items.Authors: Elsa Huby, Sébastien Vievard, Sylvestre Lacour, Olivier Guyon, Manon Lallement, Mathias Nowak, Yoo Jung Kim, Aidan Walk, Jehanne Sarrazin, Sergio Leon-Saval, Christopher Betters, Julien Lozi, Miles Lucas, Vincent Deo, Michael Fitzgerald, Barnaby Norris, Thayne Currie, Guy Perrin
Items.Title: FIRST-PL: On-sky commissioning of a visible photonic lantern for high angular resolution spectro-imaging on Subaru/SCExAO
Items.Abstract: FIRST-PL is a post-ExAO instrument on the SCExAO platform at the Subaru Telescope, to be commissioned early 2026. The PL is a multi-mode fiber transitioning into 19 single-mode fibers, placed in the focal plane to couple the telescope beam efficiently. The 19 outputs are imaged and dispersed at a spectral resolution of 3000 over 630–790 nm. The PL response depends on the input wavefront, producing distinct flux distributions for an on-axis star and an off-axis companion. By calibrating this spatial response and inverting the model, images can be reconstructed at each spectral channel, enabling integral-field capabilities at very high angular resolution. Several observing modes are offered, enabling ultra-precise spectro-astrometry on the Halpha line and image reconstruction, including Halpha differential imaging. We will present the on-sky demonstration of FIRST-PL, covering sensitivity and contrast limits as well as the expected performance for each of these observing modes.

Items.Authors: Francesco Berrilli, Luca Giovannelli, Dario Del Moro, Archana Giri Nair, Letizia Casara, Matteo Cantoresi, Valerio Di Tana, Francesco Iovanna, Antonio Turi, Laura Marcelli, Marco Casolino, Enzo Reali, Fabio Curti, Mark Anthony De Guzman, Alessandro Rossi, Matteo Marmonti, Massimiliano Musazzi, Matteo Cilia, Alessandro Turchi, Daniele Urban, Silvia Natalucci, Simone Illiano, Rita Carpentiero, Elisabetta Cavazzuti, Alberto Fedele, Alessio Di Salvo
Items.Title: SEE: a CubeSat to study solar activity and space weather
Items.Abstract: The Sun cubE onE (SEE) is a 12U CubeSat mission in LEO that will investigate UV solar emission and Gamma and X-ray fluxes to support studies in Sun-Earth interaction and Space Weather. The mission's development, part of the Italian Space Agency's ALCOR program, is handled by a team that includes the University of Rome Tor Vergata, Sapienza University, INFN, Argotec, Optec, and NEXT. SEE's objective is to monitor the emission of solar flares, from soft-X to Gamma rays, and the solar activity through images of the Sun in the Mg II doublet (280 nm). SEE mission will study Gamma and X-ray fluxes with unprecedented temporal resolution and a multi-wavelength approach, utilizing combined silicon photodiode and SiPM-based detectors. The payload will explore the flare spectrum from the keV to MeV range at a high cadence of over 10 kHz. Additionally, a UV telescope will observe the evolution of solar disk UV emission throughout part of the solar cycle and during flares.

Items.Authors: Matthew C. DeMartino, Kevin Bundy, Stephen Eikenberry, Aditya Sengupta, Anna Gagnebin, Avi Patel, Tara Crowe, Caleb Dobias, Rodrigo Amezcua Correa, Stephanos Yerolatsitis, Holger Schmidt
Items.Title: Neural-network spectral reconstruction with photonic lanterns
Items.Abstract: We investigate photonic lanterns as compact, fiber-based spectrometers, using neural networks to reconstruct spectra from single-mode output intensity patterns. Unlike conventional dispersive optics, our approach directly maps lantern outputs to input spectra via a PyTorch feedforward network with residual connections. A testbed with near-monochromatic light and reference spectra enabled training on multi-feature inputs. In the optical regime (650–700 nm), single-feature reconstructions achieved correlations near 0.99; multi-feature cases with two components reached 0.50–0.60, with greater variability for six features due to limited training data. Extending to short-wave infrared (1300–1450 nm), results remained comparable despite detector noise. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of lantern-based spectroscopy and establish a framework for neural-network spectral reconstruction, with future work focused on larger datasets and improved architectures.

Items.Authors: Erin Holdorf, Noelia Martínez Rey, Jesse Cranney, Domenico Bonaccini-Calia
Items.Title: The performance of the Smartt-WFS with machine learning in simulation and lab bench testing
Items.Abstract: Adaptive optics (AO) is a technique increasingly used in demanding applications such as free-space optical communication. In these cases, AO systems may be required to work in urban environments as well as during the daytime, where turbulence conditions worsen and scintillation increases. Traditional slope-based wavefront sensors (WFSs) degrade performance when strong scintillation is present. To overcome this challenge and achieve accurate phase estimation in strong turbulence, we are investigating the use of a new type of WFS, the Smartt-WFS (S-WFS). This WFS has been shown to have stable performance for increasing scintillation, however, at the cost of a smaller linear range. We have investigated machine learning as a method to overcome the small linear range and allow the WFS to operate in much stronger turbulence conditions. We will present the performance of the S-WFS using a machine learning reconstructor in both simulation and in lab bench testing.

Items.Authors: Dimitri P. Mawet, Clarissa R. Do Ó, Kane M. Sjoberg, Luke Lamitina, Susan F. Redmond, John G. Hagopian
Items.Title: Advancing the apodized vortex coronagraph toward Habitable Worlds Observatory requirements
Items.Abstract: The Apodized Vortex Coronagraph (AVC) is a leading architecture for high-contrast imaging on segmented telescopes and a key candidate for the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO). Building on our previous optimization of the Amplitude-Apodized Vortex Coronagraph (AAVC) for HWO’s Exploratory Cases 1 and 2, we now report progress from modeling to experiment. We present updated apodizer designs, refined sensitivity analyses, and the first laboratory implementation of the AAVC on a high-contrast testbed. Initial measurements show improved contrast performance and validate the expected error-budget trends toward the ~1e-10 requirement. We also provide updated yield estimates from FRIDAY across recent HWO aperture configurations. These results mark a key step in advancing the AAVC toward HWO requirements.
